Lucy is stressed, as she has to make an important speech at a conference and has nobody to help her write it. Sensing an opportunity to impress her, Lee offers his services, which upsets Tim, who also thinks he is the best man for the job.

It is the national finals of 'Great British Menu'. Before cooking starts the eight champions are called to London's Southbank to get a sight of the prize, the chance to cook at a banquet held at the Palace of Westminster, in celebration of everyday Great Britons honoured by the Queen. It has a huge impact on every one of the chefs, each is determined to do all he can to get a dish to the banquet.

It's day two of the national finals, and the eight champions cook their fish courses. This year's challenge has been to produce dishes that are a lasting legacy to the New Elizabethan Age. They must showcase the transformation in British cuisine during the Queen's historic 64-year reign.

It's main course day, the one course every chef wants to cook at the banquet. The chefs' dishes will be judged by Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton along with guest judge John Williams MBE, executive chef of The Ritz.

It's the final day of the competition, and the last chance for the eight champions to get one of their dishes to the banquet for Queen Elizabeth II's Great Britons. Judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton will judge the dessert course and then decide on the banquet menu to be served at the Houses of Parliament. Joining them in the judging chamber is Grace Dent, restaurant critic, journalist and author.

The winning chefs arrive at the Palace of Westminster to cook for the Banquet of Great Britons. The chefs have been selected because their dishes showcase contemporary British cuisine and demonstrate the transformation in British food during the Queen's historic reign.

Competing for top spot are Danny Parker, head chef at Michelin starred 'House of Tides' in Newcastle, who is back to try his luck in the competition again after being knocked out in the regional heat last year following a tense tie-break. He's taking on two newcomers: Dan Fletcher, protégé of Phil Howard, and now head chef at 'Fenchurch' in the City of London, and David Coulson, who runs 'Peace and Loaf' in Newcastle, which boasts 2 AA rosettes.

After a tense starter course the chefs are all aiming for 10s with their unique fish dishes. David is celebrating a personal connection to the brief with his `My Cod I Bet Me Ma'am Has Seen Some Trotters', a tribute to his mum who has worked as a chiropodist. Dan's `For All Those Sleepless Nights' pays tribute to night shift workers from the NHS with some bold but classic flavours while Danny's `Not All Superheroes Wear Capes' aims to give a taste of luxury to the hardworking staff.

Dan pays tribute to an icon of modern nursing, Florence Nightingale, while Danny is inspired by the founder of the NHS, Aneurin Bevan. David's dish is dedicated to the air ambulance staff who saved the life of his fiancé, and he even takes a trip to meet one of them.

It's the chefs' last chance to impress and tensions are high. Dan takes a risk with an unusual combination of ewe's milk and bergamot while Danny is determined to pull out all the stops with his complex dessert `Aunty Gwen's Chocolate'. David hopes to transform a childhood comfort classic into a show stopping dessert. Dan also takes a trip to meet Dr Ben Clarke who was working in the Royal London Hospital A&E during the London Bridge terror attack.
The two remaining North East chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they serve their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Banquet champion Selin Kiazim, a rising star of the London scene renowned for her Turkish Cypriot fusion flavours, is back hoping to join the elite group of chefs who have made it to the banquet twice. She is up against James Cochran who's worked at some of London's toughest kitchens including 2 Michelin starred 'The Ledbury' and Scott Goss from 'The Twenty Six' in Tunbridge Wells, renowned for his use of local Kent ingredients.

The chefs do battle for the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen is tense. Lobster is catch of the day for James whose dish is Caribbean-inspired. Scott is attempting to elevate a classic fish pie, dedicated to his mum who worked as a pharmacist in the NHS for 23 years. And Selin is taking a risk with a complex three-part fish dish featuring sardines, scallops and langoustines, as a nod to the purported health benefits of a Mediterranean diet.

Scott is showcasing rare-breed Tamworth pork to say thank you to the rare breed of people who work for the NHS. Selin is serving a complex duck dish using ingredients from all around the world to honour `Our Global NHS'. And James is presenting five cuts of goat cooked in five different ways, for his bold dish `Under The Knife'.

Selin puts her own unique twist on tea and toast. James creates a decadent coconut parfait accompanied by mango purée filled doughnuts for his dessert 'Tree of Life' inspired by the coconut palm tree, the NHS and both of their contributions to our health. Scott hopes his elevated gypsy tart 'Honey Bee Good' will secure him a place in the final.
The two remaining London and the south-east chefs must cook their four-course menus again, but will they take on board their veteran's advice as they remake their 'Feast To Say Thank You'?

Vying to be crowned champion of Scotland are three newcomers to the GBM kitchen. Lorna McNee is a former Scottish Chef of the Year and is renowned for her technical precision, gained from working at two-Michelin-starred restaurant 'Andrew Fairlie'.

It is the fish course and the chefs are all out to impress. The heat is increased as all three serve their unique takes on lobster. Ross seeks victory with his dish 'Lobster Aid'. Lorna's 'Live Well, Live Very Well' features only three elements.

Ross is hoping to impress with 'Oh Deer It's Time For Your Penicillin', his tribute to Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming featuring an unusual yeast element as well as venison. Across the kitchen, Lorna, a former Game Chef of the Year, is also cooking venison in a bid to impress.

Ross is attempting to elevate a classic into a dish worthy of the banquet, Lorna is cooking a personal tribute to NHS staff using unusual yuzu and tonka bean flavours, and Ben is serving an experimental dish which includes a beeswax ice cream.

It is judging day and the two remaining chefs must impress the panel of Oliver Peyton, Andi Oliver and Matthew Fort. Both chefs are gunning for success and are doing everything they can to deliver their menus to perfection.

Three chefs compete in the heat for the central region. Returner Ryan Simson-Trotman, who failed to reach the national finals last year, is originally from Nuneaton and opened his own restaurant Orwells in the Oxfordshire countryside with his partner Liam, who is also a contestant in the North West region.

It is the fish course and the chefs are pulling out all the stops. Marianne pays tribute to the `angels' in her local hospital who looked after her during a recent illness, and Ryan's dish is a reference to the purported health benefits of fish high in omega 3 oils, while Sabrina is inspired by her aunt, a retired nurse who used to take in food to share with her fellow workers during her shifts.

The chefs cook their mains and, following the previous day's results, tension is high. Both Marianne and Ryan are cooking muntjac in the hope of impressing the veteran judge, while Sabrina is making an ambitious technical take on a family feast.

With one dish left to impress the veteran judge, the chefs cook their desserts. Marianne is looking to raise a smile with her 'carry on' themed dessert, complete with surprise presentation. Sabrina hopes to make it through with an elevated take on jelly and ice cream while Ryan goes all out with his very sweet treat 'A Spoonful of Sugar'.

The two remaining central region chefs do battle for a place in the national finals. They must impress the formidable panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton with their four-course menus.

Andrew is attempting to pay tribute to NHS staff with his take on a traditional healing recipe, 'Mum's Flu-Fighting Chicken Soup'. Jason's 'A Tea From The Heart' is a play on a post-war remedy which harks back to the era when the NHS was formed.

After the starter results, the chefs return to the kitchen hoping for high scores with their fish dishes. Chris once again is using ingredients he has foraged from around his restaurant, while Jason hopes to impress with a spicy scallop dish and Andrew prepares a cod dish with 11 different elements.

The chefs are pulling out all the stops in a bid for big scores with their mains. All three dishes pay tribute to the founder of the NHS Aneurin Bevan, Chris's 'Everything But The Squeal' is an ambitious pork sharing platter, while Jason's 'For The Rich And The Poor' showcases lamb, and Andrew is hoping to impress with 'Aneurin Bevan For Better Steak'.

It is the dessert course and the last opportunity for the chefs to impress. Chris is hoping to triumph with another dish which showcases the foraged ingredients available around his restaurant, while Jason attempts a technical feat in his dessert inspired by a childhood hospital stay and Andrew is inspired by a dish by his great-grandmother used to cook. Which two will make it through to the judging chamber?

It is the Wales regional final as the two remaining chefs do everything they can to impress the judging panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. After tensions ran high in the week, the chefs are under pressure to deliver perfection. The judges are joined by Aneira Thomas, the first baby born on the NHS, who is named in tribute to the service's founder Aneurin Bevan and who went on to dedicate her life to the service. Who will win a place in the national finals?

It's the turn of three chefs representing the south-west, including two who have competed before but meet in the kitchen this week for the very first time. The chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their celebratory starters.

It's the fish course and with Tom renowned as a fish specialist all eyes are on him. He's cooking his take on a classic British fish supper in tribute to a charity which looks after the health of local fishermen. Jude is attempting a complex fusion dish featuring four different fish and an unusual X-Ray themed presentation, while Olivia is paying tribute to the staff who looked after her during the birth of her first son with her take on curried monkfish.

It's the main course and two of the chefs are hoping duck will win the day. Tom is preparing a technically challenging duck dish steeped in NHS history while Jude is making a multi-element Chinese duck dish inspired by his mum. Olivia is hoping her dish, using two unusual cuts of beef, will score top points. Olivia also visits her local children's hospital, home of the second-busiest paediatric A&E in the country.

With just one more chance to impress their veteran judge, the chefs are all hoping to use their pastry skills to deliver technically complex desserts. Tom's cooking an 'Invalid Fruit Tart' inspired by a 1950s recipe, while Jude is making six different apple elements for his 'An Apple A Day'. Olivia is using stout in reference to an outdated old wives' tale which suggested the drink was a healthy source of iron during pregnancy.

It's time for the two remaining chefs representing the South West to go head-to-head as they cook their menus again for the exacting panel of Andi Oliver, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. With a spot in the National Finals at stake, both are aiming for perfection as they bid for glory. The judges are joined by Barbara Childs, a Matron in the Cardiac Intensive Care Unit at Great Ormond Street Hospital, who isn't afraid to speak her mind in the chamber.

Three chefs take to the kitchen in a bid to represent the north-west in the national final. They include Ellis Barrie, from the award-winning Marram Grass in Anglesey, Liam Simpson-Trotman, an accomplished pastry chef and co-owner of the 4 AA rosette Orwell's in Oxfordshire, and Craig Sherrington, who sharpened his skills working under top names including Eric Chavot and is now Chef Patron of Virginia House in Cumbria.

It's the fish course and the chefs are all gunning for tens. Craig pays tribute to a friend who has revolutionised hospital food in Morecambe Bay, while Liam is inspired by health advice his grandma gave him and Ellis is dedicating his dish to the staff who delivered his son Albert. With cod, mackerel, shrimp and cockles on the menu, which of the chefs will score highly?

Time for the chefs to cook their mains and the pressure is on. Craig is hoping to impress using two cuts of Dexter beef, while Liam prepares his take on a Bajan lamb stew and Ellis prepares four cuts of suckling pig. Liam meets his personal hero, Nola Ishmael OBE, who became the UK's first ever black Director of Nursing.

It's the dessert course and the last chance for the North West chefs to impress in a bid to make it through to the regional final. Liam is cooking 'Not So Hot Toddy' in honour of a friend who works night shifts in the NHS, while Ellis' 'Worth Their Weight in Gold' is dedicated to the staff who saved his brother's life and Craig's dish 'The Missed Celebration' pays tribute to his wife with an unusual Christmas concept.

The two highest scoring chefs from the week return to cook their menus again. Judging them are Matthew Fort, Oliver Peyton and Andi Oliver who are joined by Dr Jake Dunning MBE, an infectious disease specialist who has been recognised for his work during the West Africa Ebola epidemic.

A helicopter rescue aboard a tanker ship, a race to save a victim who's fallen off the edge of a cliff, and a bush plane crashes just miles from the base.
US veterans tell of the quagmire they faced during the late 1960s through to the war's conclusion in 1975 and beyond when post-war developments affected Vietnamese and US affairs.
In 1864 wealthy banker Thomas Briggs was the first murder victim on a British railway.
A former gunslinger takes up arms against his brother's killer.
Taking the viewer back in time with a look at news headlines from this week, back then.
John Cannon drives gold seekers from an abandoned mine on his land, and they take vengeance by planning to kill the Cannons.
Fiona and Jesse fear for Michael's life when he must expose his true identity to James and Sonya. Meanwhile, Fiona, Sam and Jesse form a plan to retrieve Michael and save his life.
Michael must win back the trust of everyone he betrayed as James becomes obsessed with ending his life.

A fashion designer and political activist prepares to open her first flagship store, when she discovers one of her employees has been murdered. She sets out to uncover the culprits, who plan to destroy everything she has created - and also intend to kill her teenage daughter.
Jonas and the team must travel through enemy territory to bring a bride to her groom, preserving a truce between two warring Afghan tribes; Kim and Bob try to expose a man linked to terrorists.

Three Midwestern brothers, a crime lord, and an incorruptible police officer are on a deadly collision course when the youngest brother's fiancée is kidnapped by human traffickers. To save her, the MacGregor boys call on their military training and the strength of family to fight the most important battle of their lives.

Almost ten years after Megan Washington won a career-defining case as a prosecutor, putting William McCauley behind bars for the murder of his wife, new evidence emerges, the conviction is overturned, and the case is reopened. As Megan investigates, she unearths a mystery long since buried and uncovers a secret that could cost her career, her relationship and possibly her life.
After being blackmailed into taking an entrance exam for her cousin, a young woman believes that her slate is clean. However, the cousin has even darker plans for her.
Mark investigates the death of a 99-year-old millionaire who he suspects was murdered by one of his three children.
When crime reporter Ruby Herring receives clues to a murder that happened five years earlier involving a local psychic, she joins forces with Detective Jake Killian to help crack the case.
A character created by Jessica for a children's story becomes the puppet star of a children's TV show and a killer.
When Jessica is arrested for murder, secret agent Michael Hagarty and her nephew Grady conspire to keep her safely in jail while they seek the real killer.
Eliot lets Carrie and Al use his beach house in the Hamptons in exchange for help with a murder investigation, but exposing secrets in the tight-knit community ends up being challenging.
A former high line thief from Boston tries to give up crime for the sake of his teenage son, and Mary and Marshall search for the person who nearly killed Mary.
When a rising young pop star is found dead in an alley, Castle and Beckett delve into the victim's out-of-control hard-partying lifestyle, but as they dig deeper, a shocking revelation is unearthed.
When a popular illusionist dies during his magic act, Dr Sloan believes he was murdered and suspects his former partner of the crime.
Dr Sloan searches for the killer of a dance studio owner to clear the name of his friend, a dancer who is the prime suspect.
Jessica Fletcher investigates the death of a private detective found floating in the swimming pool of her publisher.
Crime writer Jessica Fletcher continues to investigate the death of a private detective found floating in the swimming pool of her publisher.

When an employee at a fashion magazine is found dead, Castle and Beckett must dive into the world of high fashion to investigate and Beckett's history in the modelling world earns her access to a wedding surprise.
A cybercriminal traps Eliot, the mayor and a businessman in a lift for ransom. Carrie must race against the clock to stop the trio plummeting to their deaths.
A break-in threatens the security of the first witnesses Mary and Marshall handled together, prompting flashbacks to the way Mary joined WitSec.
When surfer Cat Chambers returns home to The Reef, she finds herself entangled in a kidnapping when the daughter of the island's most prominent resident goes missing.
When modern-day pirates hijack a yacht and steal a laptop containing information that could take down the governor, Cat jumps into action and finds more than she expected.
Former prosecutor, Hailey Dean, is now a therapist. When her patient is questioned about the sudden deaths of her parents, Hailey's previous job will come in handy to prove her innocence.

Allied forces converge on Germany, uncovering the horrors of Belsen and Buchenwald, before pushing towards Berlin, where Adolf Hitler is clinging to power in his last desperate days.
The attack on Pearl Harbour brought the country nicknamed the 'sleeping giant', aka America, into the war, and saw the emergence of the aircraft carrier as the pre-eminent weapon of the seas.

Italian dictator Benito Mussolini dreamed of recreating the Roman Empire and making the Mediterranean the centre of a new vast colonial empire, including British-controlled Egypt and Sudan to the south.

With their armies fully engaged on the battlegrounds, the Allied and Axis powers focused their efforts to develop new weapons and new strategies to deliver a knockout blow to the enemy and bring about a quick end to the conflict.
After Hitler's gamble in the East fails, the Soviet Union starts to slowly push back and grow.
Following the days of the last World War, with a focus on Allies' strategy tensions.
Exploring the power struggle between Soviet Union, Britain, and USA for peace, following a chronological order to track their fortunes as a new world order is established.

By early 1944, Hitler had long been expecting an Allied attack on north-western France, but his problem was knowing when and where it would come. This episode has a look at the Allied operations Bodyguard and Overlord.
Concentrates on Hitler's attempts to shift the balance of power back in his favour.
The war in the Pacific against Japan was a savage hand-to-hand, island-to-island struggle, fought by new specialist fighting units like the valiant Chindits.
With Germany finally beaten, the Allies have now turned their attention to Japan, who made them pay for every inch of gained ground. Find out how this last, great foe was overcome.

Guernsey, the only British isle occupied by Nazi Germany during WWII, reveals unique wartime history.

A veteran comes to the rescue for a crew that has lost a valuable clam dredge in stormy waters. Unable to fish without it, their livelihoods are at stake.
Phil Risko's team work to re-float a trawler that has been blown onto a national park's shore, improvising to get it back to sea before it suffers further damage.

Professor Alice Roberts explores the English Civil War through the history of Oxford, the city at the heart of a battle between an autocratic king and his rebellious parliament. Oxford became the power base for Charles I and his royalist supporters.

Professor Alice Roberts tells the story of Edwardian Britain by visiting Cardiff, which grew rich selling the coal that powered the Empire. Alice hears the stories of the Edwardian miners and their backbreaking and often dangerous work.
In 1917, two ships collided in Halifax harbour, resulting in the largest man-made, non-nuclear explosion in history.
For decades, residents in Nova Scotia have reported munitions washing up on their shores, believed to have come from the wreck of the SS Clare Lilley.
Alice investigates what life was like in pre-Roman Britain. Relying on archaeology, she examines the two Hebridean Bronze Age skeletons known as the Cladh Hallan mummies.

Dr Alice Roberts goes in search of our elusive Stone Age ancestors. Along the way she visits the Channel island of Jersey where she meets a team of archaeologists hoping to shed new light on the much-maligned Neanderthals, and embarks on a kayak survey of the coastline looking for undiscovered sites hidden in the cliffs. At the Natural history museum Alice sees the dark side of our Ice Age ancestors lives.
From rural Spain in the 1800s to Russia during World War II, uncover the origins of the curses surrounding Goya's haunting 'Black Paintings', the opulent Amber Room, and more.
Exploring India at the time of the Mughal Empire, the ancient Assyrian city of Nineveh, and the mysterious origins of the curses surrounding the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

Tony Robinson heads off for a 45-mile walk across Wiltshire to tell the story of life and death in the last centuries of the Stone Age. His route takes him through the greatest concentration of prehistoric sites in Europe.

It was 30 years after the Romans invaded Britain that they were ready to take on the challenge of conquering the Lake District. Tony Robinson tracks their 50-mile walk from Penrith past Ullswater to Ambleside and on to the Irish Sea at Ravenglass.
Hugh Dennis and a team of expert archaeologists attempt to uncover a Roman fort connected to Hadrian's Wall in Benwell in Newcastle.
Hugh Dennis and a team of expert archaeologists attempt to uncover a Viking burial ground hidden beneath Masham in North Yorkshire.

Finds include: revelations from 'Britain's Pompeii', the 3,000-year-old perfectly preserved village in Cambridgeshire, including how Bronze Age ancestors designed their homes, and their kitchens packed with food and equipment, and the theatre where Shakespeare premiered Romeo and Juliet and Henry V.

A look at the camp from which Vikings invaded Britain, and groundbreaking evidence that the world-famous Avebury stone circle isn't just a sacred site but a place where people lived and worked. In Staffordshire, the oldest Iron Age gold in Britain is unearthed.

Andy embarks on an enchanting journey to a haunted bookshop once graced by Charles Dickens, investigates the captivating mystery of King John's missing bones, and delves into the intriguing rumours of Oliver Cromwell's deal with the devil.

Andy embarks on a journey back to Scotland, exploring Rosslyn Chapel and its intriguing connection to the Holy Grail. He meets Billy Kirkwood at a cave believed to house a legendary beast and uncovers the story of Scotland's most infamous witch.

Some believe a UFO was shot down by the RAF above South Wales on the 26th of February 2016. Craig and Sarah Cruddas examine the evidence as they try to discover if it really was an extra-terrestrial event, and if there's been a top level cover up.

Craig and Sarah have a closer look at a case that took place in November 2018 off the west coast of Ireland, in which pilots saw bizarre lights through their cockpit windows. The interaction with air traffic control provides the evidence.
Ein Paar hat in Daytona Beach, Florida, eine in die Jahre gekommene Wohnung direkt am Wasser gefunden und möchte sie in ein entspanntes Feriendomizil verwandeln.

Ein Paar aus Washington, D.C., ist auf der Suche nach einem erschwinglichen Strandhaus an der Chesapeake Bay in Maryland. Doch bei den ersten Abrissarbeiten stoßen sie auf ein unerwartetes Problem, das ihr Budget übersteigen könnte.

Vermieter aus Brooklyn suchen nach ihrer nächsten Anlageimmobilie in St. Thomas, wo sie die kalten Winter hinter sich lassen und ihr Geschäft vom Strand aus betreiben können. Sie sind sogar bereit, eine renovierungsbedürftige Immobilie zu übernehmen.

Ein Ehepaar aus Tennessee will sich auf St. Thomas einen lang gehegten Inseltraum erfüllen. Während ihre Kinder sich vor allem ein Haus in direkter Strandnähe wünschen, schwärmen die Eltern von der atemberaubenden Aussicht auf das türkisblaue Meer.

Ein kalifornisches Paar hat sich auf einer Kreuzfahrt Hals über Kopf in St. Thomas verliebt. Sie träumen davon, den dichten Verkehr der Bay Area hinter sich zu lassen und stattdessen morgens mit den Füßen im Sand aufzuwachen.

Eine Familie aus Wisconsin möchte ihre Kinder näher an ihre Wurzeln heranführen und zieht nach Puerto Rico. Dort sollen die Kinder die Kultur und die Erinnerungen ihrer Mutter aus Kindertagen erleben und weitertragen können.

Eine junge New Yorkerin hat genug vom hektischen Stadtleben und möchte mehr Zeit an den Stränden von Cabo Rojo verbringen. Statt weiterhin bei der Familie zu übernachten, wünscht sie sich eine moderne eigene Wohnung in Strandnähe.

Ein Paar aus Ohio träumt von einem Neustart in Punta Cana, Dominikanische Republik. Dort wünschen sie sich eine moderne Eigentumswohnung mit direktem Strandzugang, Privatsphäre und genug Platz für Freunde und Familie, die zu Besuch kommen.

Ein Paar zieht mit seinen drei Hunden nach Kreta, Griechenland. Nach diversen Umzügen verkaufen die beiden ihr Traumhaus in Alabama. Während sie von einem traditionellen Haus mit Pool und Meerblick träumt, wünscht er sich eine zentrale Lage.

Alan hat als ehemaliger Offizier der US-Marine in den letzten 30 Jahren die ganze Welt bereist. Als er 2005 in Sizilien stationiert war, lernte er Michela kennen. Das Paar heiratete und ging zurück in die USA, wo ihre beiden Kinder geboren wurden. Nachdem sie jahrelang in den USA gelebt hatten, beschlossen sie, in Michelas Heimatland zurückzukehren. Wird die Familie ein Haus finden, in dem sie Wurzeln schlagen können?

Kelly und Jennifer, zwei abenteuerlustige Freundinnen, können dank ihres Jobs als Online-Englischlehrerinnen überall auf der Welt leben. Nachdem sie ein Jahr lang zusammen gereist waren, beschlossen sie, ein Risiko einzugehen und eine Immobilie zu kaufen, um die Mittelmeerküste zu ihrem neuen Zuhause zu machen. Das erschwingliche Albanien wurde zur Heimat ihrer Träume. Werden sie ihren Traum vom Leben in Albanien verwirklichen können?

Joanna teilt das klassische libanesische Gericht ihres Großvaters, Fatayer, begleitet von einem libanesischen Salat, Hummus und Baklava als Dessert. Zum Schluss überrascht sie ihren Vater mit den Resten seines Lieblingsgerichts.

Zu den Lieblingsspeisen der Gaines-Familie während hektischer Zeiten gehören Parmesan-Hühnchen und Fettuccine Alfredo. Kombiniert werden diese Gerichte mit einem knackigen Rucola-Salat, der Frische und Leichtigkeit bringt.

Joanna kreiert ein gemütliches Friendsgiving-Essen: ein reichhaltiger Auflauf, begleitet von herzhafter Preiselbeersauce und knusprigen grünen Bohnen Amandine. Als süßer Abschluss begeistert ein fruchtiger Kirsch-Mandel-Crisp.

Chip und Crew kommen vorbei, während Joanna leckere Snacks für das Wochenende vorbereitet: French Onion Dip, Hasselback Potatoes und Erdnussbutter-Brownies. Später hilft Tochter Ella beim Philly Cheesesteak, dem Hauptgericht.

Nach dem Sammeln frischer Eier verrät Joanna das Geheimnis ihrer perfekten buttrigen Biskuits. Ob als süßer Erdbeerkuchen, herzhaft mit Wurst oder als Basis für Eggs Benedict - ihr Teig erweist sich als vielseitiger Alleskönner in der Küche.

Ein ungenutzter Raum voller Fundstücke und alter Möbel soll endlich ein Rückzugsort werden, an dem ein Paar gemeinsam Zeit verbringen kann. Jenni Yolo entwickelt aus der Sammelstelle einen gemütlichen, durchdachten Raum.

Eine junge Grafikdesignerin, die sich für Mid-Century-Design interessiert, möchte ihr erstes Haus kaufen. Ben und Erin präsentieren ihr zwei Optionen, die beide ihre Liebe zu verschiedenen natürlichen Elementen befriedigen sollen.
Drei Geschwister kehren nach Laurel zurück, um einen Ort für ihre Familien zu finden.

Ein Paar, das sein ganzes Leben auf Inseln gelebt hat, ist bereit, sich zu verkleinern. Ben und Erin zeigen ihnen Renovierungsmöglichkeiten für zwei Häuser, die sie in ein gemütliches Zuhause verwandeln können, das ihren Bedürfnissen entspricht.

Ein Paar auf der Suche nach einem Neuanfang beschließt, dass Laurel der perfekte Ort ist, möchte aber noch vor Weihnachten in die neue Wohnung einziehen. Ben und Erin präsentieren ihnen zwei Häuser, die etwas Arbeit benötigen.

Christina hilft ihrem Freund Pando, den sie bei Flip oder Flop kennenlernte, beim Zusammenzug mit seiner Freundin Michelle. Michelle zieht in Pandos Haus und zwei Stile und Geschmäcker müssen in Einklang gebracht werden.
Die Haussuche von Christina in Newport Beach beginnt offiziell, als sie und ihr Verlobter Ant beschließen, zusammenzuziehen. Beide haben Wünsche, die erfüllt werden wollen.

Eine viel beschäftigte Mutter von drei Söhnen braucht eine neue Küche. Sie wünscht sich von Christina - passend zum Rest des Hauses - einen luftigen Raum mit Strand-Feeling, der in blauen und grauen Farbtönen gehalten ist. Die Interior-Expertin setzt die Wünsche ihrer Kundin um und erneuert die komplette Küche mit Wow-Faktor.

Christina möchte ihrer besten Freundin bei der Renovierung ihrer Küche und ihres Wohnzimmers helfen. Allerdings fällt ihnen schnell auf, dass der zweite Stock nicht mehr ganz zum Rest passt. Außerdem kommen sie an die Grenzen des Budgets.

Christina kehrt nach der Geburt ihres dritten Kindes wieder zu ihrer Arbeit zurück und hilft einem Paar eine helle, offene Küche im modernen Farmhaus-Stil zu gestalten. Jedoch muss sie aufpassen, dass sie sich nicht mit ihren Aufgaben übernimmt.

Christina hilft ihrer guten Freundin, der Food Coachin Cara und ihrem Mann Chris, das gemeinsame Schlafzimmer und Bad zu renovieren. Cara dreht Ernährungsvideos in ihrem Schlafzimmer und benötigt dafür einen schönen neuen Hintergrund.

Brian und Mika stehen vor einer außergewöhnlichen Aufgabe: Zwei Häuser sollen gleichzeitig auf demselben Grundstück entstehen. Doch damit nicht genug, denn zusätzlich wartet eine weitere Renovierung auf das Team. Zwischen Zeitdruck, Koordination und unerwarteten Problemen zeigt sich, wie herausfordernd paralleles Bauen wirklich ist.

Brian und Mika bauen für zwei Schwestern gleichzeitig jeweils ein Haus auf demselben Grundstück. Doch während der Bau läuft, zieht der schwerste Sturm, den Tampa je erlebt hat, auf. Zeitdruck und Wetterchaos bringen das Team an seine Grenzen.

Zum festlichen Staffelfinale erstrahlt das Château in winterlichem Glanz. Dick und Angel laden zu ihrem traditionellen Weihnachtsfest für alle Helfer:innen ein und bereiten aufwendige Menüs sowie liebevoll gestaltete Geschenke vor.

Daphne und Ian wollen das Spielzimmer des Schlosses umgestalten und einen kindersicheren Raum für kleine Prinzessinnen und Prinzen erschaffen. Doch dabei wollen sie den einzigartigen Charme des Schlosses nicht verlieren.

Daphne und Ian widmen sich einem neuen Projekt im Schloss: Sie wollen eine luxuriöse Schlafsuite einrichten, die dem Charme der alten Gemäuer gerecht wird. Dabei müssen sie historische Details bewahren und moderne Annehmlichkeiten schaffen.

Eine leerstehende Süßwarenfabrik wird von einem Ehepaar in ein Wohnhaus umgebaut.

Nach vielen Umzügen suchen Chris und Lindy nun ein Haus, in dem sie alt werden können. Für ein Budget von 237.000 Dollar wünschen sie sich ein 4-Zimmer-Haus, mit Platz für einen Männerraum für Chris und mit einem großen Garten für die Hunde.

Das frisch verheiratete Paar Sara und Jeff wünscht sich ein Haus mit Garten und Wohnküche in Waco. Die beiden haben ein Budget von etwa 250.000 Dollar, dafür erwarten sie außerdem drei Schlafzimmer für den geplanten Nachwuchs.

Lucy meets a primary school teacher with a basement flat in East Dulwich in London, Martin meets property developers in Ebbw Vale in Wales and Workington in Cumbria, both of whom have ambitious plans for kitchens and bathrooms.

It's a family affair for all three property projects in Port Talbot, 🎾 [Tennis] Wimbledon and Telford. A father and daughter, cousins and a father and his two stepsons tackle projects bought at auction from just over £20,000 to more than £1.2 million.

Lucy enjoys a day by the seaside visiting a two-bedroom maisonette a few steps from the water in Kent's Leysdown-on-Sea, while Martin has a look at a terraced house in Cymmer in the Welsh Valleys and a two-bedroom mid-terrace in Penkhull near Stoke.

The Pyramids of Giza could be a map of the stars. First responders bring hope during Hurricane Katrina. And an Indonesian volcano erupts in a shade of blue.

A Navy seaman experiences strange events in the heart of the Bermuda Triangle; an Air Force Staff Sergeant is confronted by an otherworldly being in Iraq; a tech sergeant discovers a haunting visitor in her air base house.

An unknown presence pulls an Armed Forces Police Officer into a living nightmare. While on a covert intelligence mission, a US Navy Officer faces a terrifying reckoning, and a Marine is warned about a deadly future while stationed at an observation post.
Drones reveal what's left of Henry Ford's American suburb in the Brazilian jungle, while clues to what killed a once-vibrant Pennsylvania mining town is discovered.

Ende 2006 ermordete Steve Wright fünf junge Frauen, die alle als Prostituierte auf den Straßen von Ipswich gearbeitet hatten. Die Suche nach ihm entwickelte sich zur größten Verbrecherjagd in der Geschichte Ostenglands.

Der Serienkiller Joachim Kroll ist als "Menschenfresser von Duisburg" bekannt. Als er 1976 endlich gefasst wird, findet die Polizei sein letztes Opfer: eine 4-Jährige, die er zerlegt hatte und im Kühlschrank und in einem Kochtopf aufbewahrte.

Ed Gein, der Schlächter von Plainfield, erinnert an Horrorfilme wie "Psycho". Als die Polizei nach einer vermissten Frau sucht, findet sie auf Geins Farm ein Horrorkabinett aus Leichenteilen, das er über zwölf Jahre zusammengestellt hatte.

Der Serienkiller Fritz Honka war über viele Jahre aktiv und misshandelte und ermordete Prostituierte. Nur zufällig wurde er gefasst, als Feuerwehrleute den Verwesungsgeruch bemerkten und dann die zerstückelten Leichen mehrerer Frauen fanden.

Beverly Allitt wird auch "Todesengel von Lincolnshire" genannt. Im Jahr 1991 entsetzte die 22-jährige Krankenschwester die Welt durch ihre Morde an Babys und Kleinkindern. Ihre Opfer fand sie auf der Kinderstation eines Krankenhauses.

Beleuchtet werden Themen aus aller Welt und es Menschen und Geschichten hinter den Schlagzeilen aus der ganzen Welt gezeigt. Berichtet wird über beispielsweise über Atomversuche, Flüchtlinge und viele weitere Ereignisse rund um den Globus.

Dein Morgen, dein Rhythmus: Das Nachrichtenmagazin begleitet die Zuschauer täglich mit verständlich eingeordneten Themen aus Politik, Wirtschaft, Sport und Service. Spannende Talks sorgen für Unterhaltung und Information.

Berichtet wird über aktuelle Themen des Tages und die wichtigsten Entwicklungen in der Welt. Zudem werden Hintergründe und Einschätzungen von Politikern und Experten geliefert und es wird zusammengefasst, was die Menschen bewegt.

Die Sendung behandelt aktuelle Wirtschafts-, Verbraucher- und Finanzthemen, erklärt Hintergründe und ordnet Entwicklungen ein. Experten und Reporter aus Frankfurt und New York berichten über Trends und Bewegungen an den Finanzmärkten.
Das Nachrichtenmagazin berichtet über die aktuellsten Ereignisse und spezielle Themen.

Start-ups gewinnen als wichtiger Impulsgeber für Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft zunehmend an Bedeutung. Dieses Magazin widmet sich in jeder Ausgabe jeweils einem Thema, das Janna Linke gemeinsam mit einem Experten von verschiedenen Seiten beleuchtet.

Die Journalistin Pinar Atalay führt persönliche Gespräche mit hochkarätigen Gästen und behandelt tiefgehende und gesellschaftlich relevante Themen, die andere oft meiden. Sie sorgt für fundierte Informationen und regt zum Nachdenken an.

Die National Security Agency ist der mächtigste Geheimdienst der Welt. Das Geschehen in ihrem Hauptquartier ist eines der bestgehüteten Geheimnisse der Neuzeit. Doch das ist nur die sichtbare Spitze eines globalen Geheimdienstnetzwerks.

Das Institut für Virologie Wuhan beherbergt Chinas einziges Labor der Biosicherheitsstufe 4 (BSL-4) und wurde errichtet, um die gefährlichsten Krankheitserreger der Welt unter strengsten Sicherheitsvorkehrungen zu erforschen.

Das Magazin widmet sich Themen, die die Menschen bewegen. Investigativjournalisten schauen dabei hinter die Kulissen und decken Missstände in Politik, Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft auf. Anschließend werden die Verantwortlichen damit konfrontiert.

Heinrich Himmler ist als eine der einflussreichsten Persönlichkeiten des Nationalsozialismus fasziniert vom Okkultismus des Altertums und von der Existenz einer mystischen, arisch-magischen Kraft der deutschen Vorfahren überzeugt.

Das San-Juan-Gebirge im US-Bundesstaat Colorado ist ein Zeugnis von zerstörten Träumen des großen Geldes durch den Goldrausch. Auch der verlassene Ort Horse Sand Fort vor der Südküste Englands weist auf eine rege Geschichte hin.

Mitten in der indischen Metropole von Delhi befindet sich ein riesiger Dschungel, wo nur noch Affen und Schakale residieren sollen. Dort verborgen befindet sich eine Ruine, versteckt vor aller Welt. Es gibt einige Legenden rund um diese Ruine.

Sie begegneten einander nie und blieben doch dauerhaft aufeinander fixiert: Hitler und Stalin. Sie stiegen auf zu Führern von Diktaturen, die an blutiger Gewalt alles übertrafen, was menschlicher Wille zur Macht bis dahin an Grausamkeit hervorgebracht hatte. Scheinbar gesichertes Wissen liefert neue Einsichten in alte Fragestellungen: Wie werden Menschen zu Diktatoren.

Die Nazis sind besessen von der Idee einer deutschen Herrenrasse. Um ihre Ideologie zu festigen, suchen sie nach Anhaltspunkten in der Vergangenheit. Der Mythos der Stadt Atlantis und ihrer einst mächtigen Bewohner passt perfekt in dieses Muster.

Neuseelands Grenzschützer und Spürhunde überwachen Einreisende, Gepäck, Post und Fracht auf Schmuggelware und Biosicherheitsrisiken. Von Auckland bis Queenstown zeigt die Doku ihre akribische Arbeit zum Schutz der Inselnation.

Die Zollbeamten am internationalen Flughafen von Christchurch verdächtigen das Gepäck eines Kanadiers. Weiterhin bemerken sie ein ungewöhnlich farbenfrohes Päckchen aus Uganda. Schließlich belügt eine Philippinerin die Beamten.
Eine Brasilianerin verhält sich verdächtig. Ein Reisender gibt den Beamten einen hilfreichen Tipp.

Die Beamten fassen einen Chinesen, der mehr Zigaretten als erlaubt transportiert. Weiterhin verdächtigen sie eine Fracht mit Kupferdraht. Es stellt sich heraus, dass dort die Droge Crystal Meth versteckt eingeschmuggelt wird.

Diese Folge der Sendung wirft einen Blick auf eine Vulkaninsel vor der Küste Taiwans mit gruseligen Ruinen aus einer dunklen Ära. Außerdem wird eine Miniatureisenbahn, die in den Wäldern von Arkansas versteckt ist, erforscht.

Diese Folge der Sendung wirft einen Blick auf das Hartwood Hospital in Lanarkshire, Schottland. Das Gebäude war einst eines der größten psychiatrischen Krankenhäuser in Europa. Experten diskutieren über die dunkle Geschichte des imposanten Gebäudes.

Die Dokumentation zeigt die im Wald gelegenen höhlenartigen Kuppelbauten in Indien, die seit ihrer Darstellung durch die Beatles als "Ashram" berühmt geworden sind. Die heute bröckelnden Bauten waren einst der Gipfel des spirituellen Luxus.

Die Demokratische Republik Kongos ist gespickt mit den Überresten einer sehr wechselhaften Regentschaft. Heruntergekommene Gebäude und ein zerfallenes Stadion gehen auf den alten Machthaber Mobutu Sese Seko zurück.

Die Schweizer Alpen sind die imposante Kulisse für die Fahrt im Bernina Express. Auf seiner Fahrt von Chur im Kanton Graubünden über das Wintersportmekka St. Moritz bis ins italienische Tirano überwindet der Zugklassiker mehr als tausend Höhenmeter.
Die Sendung zeigt eine Reise an Bord eines luxuriösen Touristenzuges durch Nordspanien.

Der ehemalige Achterbahn-Testpark in Rust zieht täglich bis zu 30.000 Gäste an. Für einen reibungslosen Ablauf und ein unvergessliches Erlebnis sorgt ein engagiertes Team aus Technikern, Reinigungskräften und Gastronomen im Hintergrund.

In dieser Sendung geht es um den "Las Vegas High Roller", der mit 167 Metern das höchste Riesenrad Nordamerikas ist. Der Bau des Rades fand an mehreren Standorten auf der ganzen Welt statt. Das Rad bietet eine atemberaubende Aussicht über Las Vegas.

In dieser Sendung geht es um die gigantische Betonkonstruktion der neuen Samuel-De-Champlain-Brücke, die über dem Sankt-Lorenz-Strom im kanadischen Quebec gebaut wurde. Täglich passieren tausende Fahrzeuge auf dieser Doppelschrägseilbrücke.

Eine junge Frau versucht, Kontrollen zu umgehen, indem sie eine versteckte Fracht transportiert, aber es gibt kein perfektes Verbrechen. Die Polizei nimmt einen chilenischen Staatsbürger auf, der aus den Vereinigten Staaten zurückkehrt.

Der Zoll kontrolliert einen Flug aus Brasilien. Im Gepäck wird ein verdächtiger Fund gemacht. Währenddessen bangt ein nervöser Peruaner um seine Einreise. Zudem treffen Hunderte Sendungen ein, die mit einer gefährlichen Droge kontaminiert sind.

Am Flughafen von Santiago de Chile erleben die Beamten einen ereignisreichen Tag: Ein Reisender aus Spanien sorgt mit überladenem Gepäck für Aufsehen - unter Kleidung und Souvenirs verbergen sich Luxusgüter in verdächtiger Menge.

Das Gepäck einer Passagierin weckt den Verdacht der Beamten. Doch erst die Röntgenuntersuchung bringt Erschreckendes ans Licht. Ein junger Mann kehrt mit Übergepäck aus Europa zurück und reagiert äußerst aggressiv auf die Kontrollen.

Erleben Sie den Polizei-Sonderwagen "Survivor R" - ein Fahrzeug für die extremsten Einsätze. Vorgestellt werden seine Technik und Fähigkeiten. Zudem wird eine Reise durch die Geschichte der gepanzerten Einsatzfahrzeuge geboten.

In dieser Reportage wird gezeigt, wie die Zollbeamten gegen den Schmuggel kämpfen. Bei der Kontrolle des grenzüberschreitenden Warenverkehrs brauchen sie Hightech-Ausrüstung und vierbeinige Spürnasen, um die Schmugglerbanden zu stoppen.

Im Jahr 1995 wird die Aachener Justizvollzugsanstalt gegründet. In den Folgejahren beherbergt sie bis zu 700 Insassen zugleich. Die Gründe für deren Inhaftierung sind grundverschieden, so auch ihre Geschichten und ihr Umgang mit dem Arrest.

Das Gefängnis "Kolonie 8" im Norden der Ukraine ist eines der härtesten und berüchtigtsten Gefängnisse des Landes. Wer in der Großstadt Schytomyr eine Strafe begeht, findet sich in diesem Gefängnis wieder, welches höchste Sicherheitsvorkehrungen hat.

In russischen Hochsicherheitsgefängnissen leben 2.000 Häftlinge mit lebenslanger Strafe, darunter Terroristen, Mafiabosse und Serienmörder. Christoph Wanner und sein Team erhalten als erste Westeuropäer Einblick und sprechen mit Wärtern und Insassen.

In der Hauptstadt Manila befindet sich das größte Frauengefängnis der Philippinen. Die Großstadt ist von Armut gezeichnet, und viele Schicksale enden in der Kriminalität. Die häufigsten Vergehen sind Betrug, Prostitution und Drogen.

Just 4 minutes after take-off from Singapore Changi Airport, on 4 November 2010, Qantas Flight 32 suffers an uncontained failure in one of its engines. The failure is the first of its kind for the Airbus A380, the world's largest passenger airliner.
Experts analyse the British Airways Flight 38 incident, in which a lack of engine power caused the plane to crash just before landing at London Heathrow Airport.
In the halls of Queen Elizabeth I's court, John Dee was both lauded as a brilliant mathematician and feared as a summoner of angels and demons.

Royal relics expose a healing ritual once believed to cure with a touch. An ancient skull reveals how far healers go to fight leprosy. And new evidence from Egypt reveals how early medicine confronted cancer.
Featuring cake pops, slice cream, tartar sauce and crunchy almonds.
An anonymous tip-off holds the key to solving the mystery when a cargo flight crashes to the ground moments after taking off from Miami.

Just a few minutes after taking off from Bucharest, Tarom's 371 flight plunges into a field. Rumblings of an onboard bomb reach a frantic tone, and Romanian investigators call the FBI to determine whether it was an accident or an act of murder.
Three real world disasters dissected; nuclear missile, ferry, oil rig.
Tim and Fuzz get help from James Nesbitt as they try to fix up one of the worst cars they have ever encountered, unsuspecting owner Billy's 1959 MGA roadster.
Drugs are found on a plane, and we see how air traffic control prevents accidents. Airport staff strut their stuff on a catwalk, but will it be a success or a fiasco?
Relive the tragedy of the unresponsive Birgenair Flight 301 that was brought crashing into the ocean off Santo Domingo by a rogue insect nest.
A platoon of Canadian tank hunters engage a column of Nazi Panther tanks at nighttime.
Archaeologists investigate Egypt's legendary pharaoh, Alexander the Great. Teams explore catacombs and temples for his legacy and his tomb.

On a steep hillside, Björn risks everything to rescue a tractor that threatens to fall. Meanwhile, Thor gets stuck in the mud after a truck sinks deep in a farmers' field. When his tow-truck can't get a grip, he must think on his feet.
More than 100 people died when a German InterCity Express train travelling at 125 mph crashed into a bridge at Eschede in 1998. How did the disaster happen?
Careening into a mountaintop just minutes from the runway, an American charter flight becomes the worst aviation disaster in Portuguese history.
The story of the Allied forces trying to free Europe by fighting Nazi fanatics until the last man is standing.
Autumn 1942: After devastating Nazi bombing raids, fierce fighting breaks out in the streets of Soviet Stalingrad in the bloodiest battle of WWII.

WWII left a huge number of ships and submarines hidden beneath the waves. As the oceans drain, each vessel tells its tale, with surveys and scans allowing for new data-based 3D reconstructions and a whole new set of explanations.

The crash of a Korean cargo plane outside London baffled investigators. Though they quickly determined the cause of the disaster, it's possible the first officer was more concerned with saving face rather than preventing the disaster from happening.
At San Juan airport, a couple returning from Colombia is diverted to secondary after officers uncover mysterious medications in their bags, prompting further investigation.

In August 1944, a British battalion encounters fierce German resistance while trying to cross the Seine River. With bridges destroyed and no tank support in sight, they must fight to secure a critical bridgehead and continue their advance.
The staff at these Alaskan conservation centres go beyond the caretaker role by forming close relationships with rescued wild animals.
The villagers of Port Protection are back to paving with good intentions.
Curly shoots a bear. Troy and Sarah struggle with a new water system.
Dr. Oakley competes in a rodeo and treats a dog with persistent nosebleeds.

Dr Pol welcomes a new vet to the clinic. Dr Pol treats a local K9 deputy's paw; Dr Nicole examines a service dog; Dr Lisa stitches up a horse; Dr Brenda soothes a cat's burnt limb; Dr Olivia jumps into action and helps Dr Lisa with a cow in labour.
A litter of motherless dhole pups seek acceptance from the pack leader under the watchful eye of the team. Meanwhile, a Chuckwalla fights for survival.
Simon and Nadine must stop a rare green Mamba from laying her eggs where they're not wanted. They also head to a pool party that's been crashed by a Burmese python.
Water sources transform from oases into battlegrounds. Predators defend shrinking pools, causing prey to risk their lives with every approach.
The caretakers at Disney's Animal Kingdom are used to dealing with all kinds of animal shenanigans.
The engineers of the Chepe Express manage to keep the train safe as it winds through the stunningly rugged terrain of Mexico's Copper Canyon.
From Antarctica's icy wilderness to Africa's golden shores, penguins brave predators and extremes to raise the next generation.
Big cats may seem like the ultimate wildlife cliché, but they're locked in a global battle for survival. Powerful and dangerous, they now clash with humans more than ever.
A special bonobo gives the vet team a scare on the way to her annual exam, and two Asian small-clawed otters show off their x-ray training skills.
A giraffe X-ray, painted dog pack checkup, plus an adorable flamingo chick!
Dr Oakley must hold her ground when she treats two rather unpredictable boars. Plus, a camel needs neutering and some baby owls get their first check up.
Lions dominate, wild dogs push back, and a leopard mother defends her cubs. Survival is fierce and unforgiving in the fight to rule the wild.
What happens when two of the world's deadliest predators go head-to-head?!
Three real-world disasters forensically dissected: Lac-Mégantic train crash, Imperial Sugar refinery explosion, and the Ever Given container ship accident.
Casey Anderson treks through this vast wilderness, taking survival tips from the rare and endangered wildlife living on the edge of the abyss.
Hyena Queen Zalika plots her revenge on the lions who keep her clan in exile. She is building an army to confront the pride but must find food to keep the growing cubs satisfied.

The breakfast show that sets the agenda for the day.

Keep track of how far the morning's stories have developed and how the rest of the day is looking.

India Global will be your window to the world where we will decode New Delhi's diplomatic moves and positions on global issues in a world that is seeing constant geopolitical shifts.
Nidhi Razdan has a discussion on young leaders and communal politics.

A Political satire show features a combination of comedy which highlights the issues of the society with some lively fun, analysis and commentary on the latest news, there will be a lot of laughter, jokes and music.
Hosts Madiha Naqvi and Shafaat Ali get weekday mornings going, featuring a combination of news, stories of the day, and covering other important issues, with key figures from all around the world.
Cover all that is happening in the international and national sports arena.

Greta Van Susteren gives the big news from D.C., N.Y., across America, and around the world.
Finnerty Weekend with straight talk on the biggest issues facing America and the world!
John Tabacco and his crew look at the big issues, and they also shine a light on the policies of the elites.
Classic celebrity roast of Bob Hope.
Raw bodycam footage capturing high-stake police incidents.
This portrait delves deeply into Presley's life and worldwide fame as a recording artist, Hollywood star and cultural icon, with rare archival footage and interviews with those who knew him best.
A chronicle of the life and career of comedy legend, Lucille Ball.

From childhood poverty, neglect and loneliness to premature death, Marilyn Monroe endured criticism, insecurities, drug dependence, miscarriages and broken marriages, yet she managed to parlay her beauty, talent and quick wit into a Hollywood career.
An examination of the conspiracy theories behind who assassinated John F. Kennedy.
An in-depth look at Mark Chapman, the man who murdered John Lennon on that fateful December day in 1980.
Live national headlines, expert interviews and insight into the stories shaping America.

Bringing breaking news, investigative reports, and political coverage.
